email.body1:
Bruce, saw SIS hit 30 years and debuted the AI-powered SIS Scribe at ASCA 2026.

A new product launch usually means more in-market surgical facilities in play than a regional rep can cover before the pipeline cools, and that is where Midwest deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for SIS off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.subject2: meetings to hit your territory number
email.body2:
Bruce, quick follow-up for SIS.

After a launch, the expectation on a territory rep tends to jump faster than the time you have to prospect it. Most reps don't actually know how many meetings the Midwest number requires, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your territory needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks without more coverage.
email.body3:
Bruce, last bit of proof for SIS.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how a focused territory's reply rate likely compares across healthcare software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Bruce, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If covering more Midwest accounts without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters, and the post-launch stretch keeps a territory busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a regional sales motion? I'll tailor it to SIS either way.
